M1: Thanks for telling me. You're the third person to mention it this morning, so it's clearly a real problem. I can't fix it from here, but I'll speak to the building's facilities manager right away. She usually sends someone to look at things like that by the end of the day.
M1: Chào buổi sáng, chào mừng đến Brightbrew Café. Tôi có thể bắt đầu nhận đơn hàng cho bạn không?

M1: Cảm ơn bạn đã cho tôi biết. Bạn là người thứ ba đề cập đến việc này sáng nay, vậy rõ ràng đây là một vấn đề thực sự. Tôi không thể sửa nó từ đây, nhưng tôi sẽ nói chuyện với quản lý cơ sở của tòa nhà ngay lập tức. Cô ấy thường cử ai đó đến xem những thứ như vậy vào cuối ngày.

M1: Hi there, welcome to the workshop. I'm Victor — what can I build for you today?

W1: Hi. I'm opening a small clinic next month, and I need a piece for the front, where patients will check in and sign forms. It should have space for two staff members behind it. I was thinking light oak. How soon could it be ready?

M1: A reception desk like that usually takes about two weeks once you've approved the design. It'll go right in the waiting area, so durability matters — oak's a good call. Before we get into measurements, come look at these wood samples so you can compare the finishes and settle on a material.

W1: Xin chào. Tôi sắp mở một phòng khám nhỏ vào tháng tới, và tôi cần một món đồ cho khu vực phía trước, nơi bệnh nhân sẽ đăng ký và ký giấy tờ. Nó cần có chỗ cho hai nhân viên phía sau. Tôi đang nghĩ đến gỗ sồi sáng màu. Bao lâu thì có thể sẵn sàng?

M1: Một quầy lễ tân như vậy thường mất khoảng hai tuần sau khi bạn đã phê duyệt thiết kế. Nó sẽ đặt ngay ở khu vực chờ, nên độ bền rất quan trọng — gỗ sồi là lựa chọn tốt. Trước khi chúng ta đi vào số đo, hãy đến xem những mẫu gỗ này để bạn có thể so sánh các lớp hoàn thiện và quyết định vật liệu.

Tolliver Clock and Watch Workshop specializes in the repair and restoration of mechanical clocks and watches, from pendulum wall clocks and mantel clocks to hand-wound and automatic wristwatches. We have served the district for more than twenty-five years.

Our benches are dedicated entirely to spring-driven mechanisms, so we do not service battery or quartz movements, and we do not carry out jewelry or eyeglass repair. Restoration of older pieces often requires small parts to be made by hand on site, and every completed repair carries a full twelve-month guarantee covering both parts and labor. How long a repair takes depends on the service it needs, as shown below.

All items must be brought to the workshop in person, as we cannot accept timepieces sent by mail. We recommend bringing any original winding keys or paperwork, although this is not required. The Selby District Chess Association will hold its annual Selby Open Championship at Riverton Civic Hall this autumn, and organizers say they expect one of the strongest turnouts in years. The Selby Open Championship was held at Riverton Civic Hall on Saturday, December 6. Leading the effort is Estelle Monroe, who spent more than fifteen years teaching art at a nearby high school before retiring three years ago. Since then she has volunteered at the center every week, and this autumn she takes charge of its expanding beginner workshop program. The Bramford Historical Society will open its new Local History Center to the public next Saturday, offering residents a permanent home for the town's records, photographs, and everyday objects. The center occupies the former Trescott Flour Mill on Bell Lane, a stone building that stood empty for nearly twenty years before volunteers restored it over two summers. The ground floor holds a reading room and a small exhibit gallery, and the upper floor has been fitted out for workshops and document storage.

"A history center is only as rich as the community that fills it," said Ronald Ashworth, the society's director. "I would encourage every household in Bramford to look through their attics and drawers and donate old letters, maps, and family photographs, so that the collection reflects the whole town."
Residents who wish to take part may bring items to the center throughout opening week or ask a volunteer about lending materials for copying. To learn more, call the society office at 555-0148.
